svg.aria-label: Catch Up! meeting space planner wireframes for laptop and tablet landscape, 1280 pixels wide
svg.title: Catch Up! — desktop and tablet-landscape wireframes (1280 px)
svg.desc: Four frames at 1280 by 800: home with a labelled dark sidebar, the create wizard with a side summary panel, the options screen as a three-pane list, map and detail layout, and the voting screen with a decision-readiness panel.
svg.text: Catch Up! — meeting space planner · LAPTOP / TABLET LANDSCAPE 1280 px
breakpoint 3 of 3 · the dark mobile top bar becomes a labelled left sidebar · Options becomes a three-pane list + map + detail with no navigation

g.text: Invited by Mia · decide by Mon 18:00 · 3 of 4 responded
⚠ 1 member has not seen this yet
Responsive change: the mobile dark top bar and the bottom tab bar merge into one labelled left sidebar, which also surfaces the saved defaults
and the signed-in identity permanently. Cards go from one column (mobile) to two (tablet) to three. Same cards, same copy, same type scale.
This frame also covers tablet landscape — 1024 px and up gets the sidebar; below that the icon rail is used instead.
D2 · Create — form plus a persistent summary panel
optional — the link works later too
Change them once, not per meeting.
Nothing is saved to the group until you continue.
Responsive change: the third of the screen that mobile cannot spare becomes a permanent summary panel, so the consequences of the form are
visible while filling it in. The form itself is the same fields in the same order.
D3 · Options — three panes, no navigation needed ◀ the layout this breakpoint exists for
One bar per member, never just
degrades one card, not the pane.
Selecting a card pans the map
The app recommends — the group decides.
D4 · Vote — live votes beside decision readiness
You can change your vote until 18:00.
Each vote is stored under your own user id, so two people voting at the same moment cannot overwrite
each other. Only the organiser can close the vote.
Closing now would decide on 3 votes.
Asks for confirmation. Everyone is notified.
Responsive change: mobile shows voting and the confirmed result as two separate screens, so an organiser has to commit before seeing the
outcome. At this width the result preview sits next to the votes, which is why the organiser-only action can be shown with its consequences.
Readiness is derived state (selectors over responses, constraints and votes) — not a new database field.
